source_sync.preserved_differences: Six existing documents retain independent history; feature headers only. The independent portability workflow receives four energy analysis lines and preserves all additional NVL checks

visual_review.scope: Eight actual screenshots manually inspected: synthetic energy panel plus installed release window on Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Rocky 8 and Rocky 10. Other captured images are archived, not all manually reviewed.
observations: Synthetic CPU 130, two disabled controls and the complete 64-bit word 0xA5C3211098780243 are legible in all four fixture windows.
Read and copy buttons, field/state selectors, Apply and the complete status/note text fit without clipping or overlap.
The installed Energy optimization tab has an empty table, an unselected disabled value and disabled Apply until an explicit read.
Intel sub-tabs use scroll arrows when necessary; the selected new tab label is fully visible.
Fixture values are synthetic test data, not hardware measurements or proof of physical energy behavior.

limits: Energy controls require Intel family 6 model B7, bare metal and MSR support; no all-core/package broadcast
MSR 1FC bit 19 Efficient Turbo and bit 20 Race to Halt use inverse enabled polarity; preserve other 63 bits
Fresh full old-value comparison and full 64-bit readback; same values skip writes; no retry or automatic rollback
No extra lock is inferred from unrelated OC/PROCHOT fields; no adjacent thermal/power control changes
Enhanced TVB, Vmax, per-core TVB, other AMD/Intel/board protocols, physical hardware and Secure Boot acceptance remain pending
Portable core validation on Windows/macOS is not a full hardware port

source_research.sources: Original complete EE_TURBO_DIS / RTH_DIS / Rd_POWER_CTL_Tuner instructions; Intel SDM Table 2-39 and pinned Raptor Lake-S FSP
source_research.adaptation: MSR 1FC disable bits 19/20; expose inverse enabled polarity, preserve other 63 bits, compare full old value and verify full readback.
source_research.original_failure: Original setters ignore failed wrapper reads/writes and may use cleared output buffers; production rejects failed reads.
